boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct Roesch Library settings for individual work, group sessions, research, and media projects.

cards.title: Gathering Place
cards.subtitle: Roesch Library, second floor
cards.notes: Set up at an open table for active work, then check the library’s reservation system if an event configuration affects the area.
cards.short_summary: An open, flexible second-floor study area that can also host events.
cards.evidence_claim: The library describes Gathering Place as an open second-floor area typically configured for active, flexible study and reservable for events.
cards.access_notes: Roesch spaces can be reserved with a UD email address; this area may also be reserved for events.

cards.title: The Collab (Room 240)
cards.subtitle: Roesch Library, second floor
cards.notes: Use this flexible classroom for a planned group session; confirm availability first because library instruction, meetings, and events may use it.
cards.short_summary: A flexible classroom for teaching, learning, meetings, and events.
cards.evidence_claim: The library identifies The Collab as Room 240, a flexible classroom primarily used for library instruction and also reservable for events and meetings.
cards.access_notes: Check reservation availability before relying on the room; it is used for instruction and may be reserved.

cards.title: Heidi's Porch
cards.subtitle: Roesch Library, first floor near leisure reading
cards.notes: Bring a reading assignment or laptop to this collaborative nook near the leisure-reading collection; choose another floor when you need quiet.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor collaborative nook beside leisure reading.
cards.evidence_claim: The library says Heidi’s Porch is near the first-floor leisure-reading collection and is a welcoming, collaborative study nook.
cards.access_notes: The first floor is designated noisy on the library floor map; food and drink are allowed in study areas.

cards.title: Roesch Retreat
cards.subtitle: Roesch Library, fifth floor
cards.notes: Use the forest-inspired retreat for quiet reading, a short reset, or contemplative work; keep conversation considerate on the fifth floor.
cards.short_summary: A fifth-floor well-being space for studying, conversation, or contemplation.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries states that Roesch Retreat is on the fifth floor and offers students space for studying, conversation, or contemplation.
cards.access_notes: The library floor map designates the fifth floor as considerate; the space includes seating and a sound machine.

cards.title: Concourse D
cards.subtitle: Roesch Library, second floor
cards.notes: Choose Concourse D for collaborative work and spread materials across a shared workspace; reserve ahead when a defined area is needed.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor collaborative space with reservable areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The library floor map lists Concourse D among the second-floor spaces, and the libraries site offers it as a reservable space.
cards.access_notes: Second-floor sound level is noisy; reserve available Concourse D space with a UD email address when needed.

cards.title: Dialogue Zone
cards.subtitle: Roesch Library, first floor
cards.notes: Use the Dialogue Zone when talking through a group assignment is part of the work, and move upstairs for a quieter concentration session.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor library setting suited to conversational work.
cards.evidence_claim: The official floor map lists Dialogue Zone as a first-floor Roesch Library space, where the designated sound level is noisy.
cards.access_notes: Located on Roesch’s noisy first floor; food and drink are allowed in study areas.

cards.title: Scholars’ Commons
cards.subtitle: Roesch Library, second floor
cards.notes: Use Scholars’ Commons as a second-floor base for laptop work or project check-ins, keeping the noisier floor designation in mind.
cards.short_summary: A named second-floor library study environment.
cards.evidence_claim: The official floor map lists Scholars’ Commons among Roesch Library’s second-floor spaces.
cards.access_notes: Second-floor sound level is noisy; look for an open table or reserve a room with a door through the library.

cards.title: Cameron Corner
cards.subtitle: Roesch Library, fifth floor
cards.notes: Pair a reading-heavy assignment with a seat in Cameron Corner, then keep voices low in the fifth floor’s considerate environment.
cards.short_summary: A fifth-floor leisure-reading area in a considerate study zone.
cards.evidence_claim: The official floor map places Cameron Corner leisure reading on Roesch Library’s fifth floor, designated considerate.
cards.access_notes: Fifth floor has a considerate sound level; library guidance says each floor has a designated noise level.

cards.title: Story Studio
cards.subtitle: Roesch Library, second floor
cards.notes: Reserve time here when coursework needs recorded or edited video; bring a USB flash drive to save project files when you finish.
cards.short_summary: A media-production studio for recording and editing video projects.
cards.evidence_claim: The Story Studio is on Roesch Library’s second floor and is described as a media-production studio for recording and editing video projects.
cards.access_notes: Use the library’s space-availability page to check or reserve the studio; the library says a USB flash drive is needed to get started.

cards.title: 4-A Study Room
cards.subtitle: Roesch Library, fourth floor
cards.notes: Reserve this two-person room for focused pair work, using its window and whiteboard to organize a problem set or planning session.
cards.short_summary: A two-person fourth-floor study room with a window and whiteboard.
cards.evidence_claim: The library’s room listing describes 4-A as a two-person fourth-floor study room with a window and whiteboard.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s availability calendar before use; dry-erase markers and erasers are available at the Hello Desk.
